title: Ruth
tagline: God's quiet faithfulness, working through ordinary people in a chaotic age, including a foreigner who became part of the story.
author: Anonymous
authorNote: Jewish tradition points to Samuel; scholars debate it. Most place the writing in the monarchy period, looking back.
audienceNote: Likely an audience that knew David's name and wanted to know where his family came from.
settingNote: A morally messy era, with famine, migration, and little central authority.
genreNote: A short story told with care. Watch the dialogue, the loyal love, and what goes unsaid.
bigIdea: Loyal love (*hesed*) shows up in small, costly choices, and God is at work in them.
mapSummary: A famine pushes a family east into Moab, a neighboring rival. A widow returns west with a Moabite daughter-in-law at her side.

scene.author: An unnamed author
scene.audience: Israel in the days of the kings
scene.happening: A famine in the days of the judges

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.
